quest.title: Now's No Time for Tears
quest.description: "Some people think I'm not enough. I have two words for those people: Think again."
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Okay, people, time to go!

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: I wonder what the Mondstadt's comic collection is like? Hehe, don't let me down, Mondstadt Library...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xilonen, we made it.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Nice, everyone's here. Let's go — Minnie and Varesa are already inside.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: I'm surprised Miss Musk isn't here today. I always see her by the linguistics section.

choices.text: Yeah, it's not like her to slack off...

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: You guys know this place inside out, huh? Even down to the regulars. That's impressive!

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Of course. The library is my secret base.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: I know which books are on what shelves, who the regular customers are, even what brand of tea Lisa uses for her afternoon drink.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: This chair is the same one I was sitting in when I first read through The Soulblazer Saga.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: And any time I want to write letters to my friends in the Legion, this is where I come.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: I just feel so comfortable here. Miss Lisa is really friendly — she's shared some of her snacks with me before.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Wow, amazing... Mmm, snacks... Hehe...

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Ahem... What I meant to say was, this library is totally different from the one back home.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Instead of books, we have woven scrolls. They're usually hung up high on the walls, which means the shorter kids can't always see them.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Heh, but I was always tall for my age. Whenever my friends wanted to read a woven scroll, they'd come get me to read it out for them.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: I got so used to reading woven scrolls in a group that when I eventually got into comics, I carried on the habit. It's more fun reading them together with friends.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: You think so? How does that work, though? 'Cause everyone reads at a different pace, right?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: It works fine. The faster readers just wait for the others to catch up before turning the page. Plus, with other people around, you can read for a bit, then chat for a bit, then read some more... Beats reading in silence!

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Funnily enough, that's actually how I got to know Xilonen.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: This one time, I came to her workshop, planning to commission her for a job. When I arrived, I found Nepecha reading a comic book — and it turned out it was The Soulblazer Saga!

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: We were both pretty stoked to meet a fellow Soulblazer fan, and I guess we were chatting so loudly that we woke Xilonen up from her nap.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: She came over, intending to quiet us down... but that turned into us roping Xilonen into reading comics with us.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Next thing you know, it was the middle of the night and we'd been at it for hours... Xilonen was so tired, she just lay down in between me and Nepecha and went to sleep. Hehe, ever since then, we've been the best of friends!

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: That sounds so nice... I really wanna meet Nepecha, too. I hope I can visit Natlan one day...

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: We can make that happen! I'm sure Xilonen would be more than happy to introduce you. And don't forget to invite me too!

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: It's just...

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Hey, don't feel down! A deal's a deal. As long as we get ranked in the contest, your parents will have to respect your wishes.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: So let's put all our energy into doing the best we can. We're gonna get that ranking, and you're gonna go on that trip!

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Mm... I'll do my best!

choices.text: Maybe she went out to find some hilichurls for her research.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: They don't seem to have a dedicated section for comics and light novels here. Everything from the Yae Publishing House is grouped under "Children and Teens"...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there something wrong with that...?

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Everything is wrong with that. Would you put The Soulblazer Saga on the same shelf as The Boar Princess?

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: Hey, watch it... What have you got against The Boar Princess, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry — I didn't mean it like that. To be fair, The Boar Princess is a pretty good read. I bought the whole set from the Wanwen Bookhouse.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you reading, Yigang?

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: The Soulblazer Saga: Armored Assault, volume 1... Ah. The Soulblazer spinoff.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Yup. This book was my first introduction to the Soulblazer universe.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: It abandons traditional modes of human combat, instead housing the heroes within giant armored mecha, each the size of the Jade Chamber.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: And since it isn't canon, it's free to delve into territory that the original series can't explore — like aerial combat. It goes pretty hard.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: When I discovered this as a boy, ahh... I thought it was the coolest thing ever. As soon as I saw mecha and mid-air dogfights, I was hooked.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: So you're big into the mecha genre, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Hehe, I sure am. After that, I was hunting down books in the Soulblazer series wherever I could find them. I even bought the mecha warrior action figures released by the Yae Publishing House.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: *sigh* I gotta say though, it really did a number on my savings. Those action figures are so expensive, and there are so many to collect.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: Yup, that's how it goes. Seems like every other day there's a Soulblazer reprint, collector's edition, spinoff series, sequel... So much to keep track of.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Yeah... The thing is, the publisher knows exactly what they're doing. They keep milking their cash cow for all it's worth, because chumps like me fall for it every single time...

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: ...Me too...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I am loving the atmosphere in here. The peace and quiet, the subtle scent of flowers in the air, plus the chairs look really comfy. Whoever runs this library has great taste.

choices.text: I wholeheartedly agree.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, that being said... what happened to actually running the library? I don't see any staff anywhere.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lisa's probably taking her afternoon break at the moment.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Afternoon break? Hmph... I'm the one who should be on an afternoon break.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ugh, that's it — Okay, I am taking a nap. You guys go hang with Varesa, I'm gonna find a table to pass out on.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Yeah, it's just too cozy here not to. It'd be a shame to waste the opportunity.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hmm... There, that table. I have been eyeing it since we got here. It has "nap material" written all over it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Does it, though?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has a funny feeling that Lisa would approve of Xilonen's commitment to afternoon naps.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: *snoring*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that was fast! One second she's talking to us, the next she's out like a light!

choices.text: Her work can't catch up with her here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess so... Happy napping, Xilonen.

choices.text: Maybe that makes it easier for her to relax.
Lisa is a woman of exceptional taste.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: My appetite is insatiable today. Must be because of all the exercise.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yeah, I bet everyone's getting hungry by now. We did push it pretty hard this morning.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: *sigh* Plus, the organizing committee had a load of supplies to distribute today. Stuff to keep people warm.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: I'm ravenous after moving all those boxes. Minnie, you're a local — any recommendations on where to get a late lunch?

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Uh... How about Good Hunter? Their steaks are really good.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Oh, I am so down. I'm, I'm... achoo... craving a plateful of meat right now.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: Yigang... don't tell me you caught a cold again?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Sounds like we should get some hot soup for the table. C'mon, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: My my, looks like a lot of visitors snuck in while I was on my afternoon break. Hello, cutie. Hello, little Paimon. It's been too long.

choices.text: We were hoping we'd catch you...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: That's quite alright. I'm sure your Natlanese friend here has read the library rules carefully and intends to abide by them.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: As for your other Natlanese friend... Hehe, I'm glad to see someone appreciates the cozy atmosphere. She looks like she's having a wonderful nap.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Now then. Has everyone decided which books they'd like to borrow?

response.speaker: Tang Yigang
response.text: Yes, Ma'am. I'd like to borrow this copy of Armored Assault.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: And I'll take this one — Vera's Melancholy. Minnie recommended it.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: No problem. What about your, um... leopard friend? Did she want to borrow a book?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Huh...? Hmm? Borrow a book? Ah... No need, thanks. This one was great, but I won't be checking it out.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Let's see... Ah, Along with Divinity. You have very good taste in books.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hehe, or should I say, good taste in pillows?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, yeah, sorry, that's my drool... Ah, sorry! Okay...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Alright, let me fill out the register, then you'll be free to take your books.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Lisa checks out the books, hands them over, and sees you all to the door.

choices.text: But you were on your break, so we just went ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Everyone loves Good Hunter. My family eats here all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: It's a little small, though. We'll probably have to split the group across two tables.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Ah, bummer... Well, never mind. We've done plenty of group activities recently, it won't kill us to split up just this once.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: Haha, Captain's already been hypnotized by the menu.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: It smells so good... Meat stew... seafood... Ahhh!

dialogues.speaker: Sara
dialogues.text: Are you ready to order?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Let's see... Um, I guess I'll get the ball rolling.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Let's start with thirty plates each of Tea Break Pancakes and Flaming Red Bolognese, seven bowls of Calla Lily Seafood Soup...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: And um... yeah, thirty Meatnados. As for appetizers... twelve Apple Roly Polies and twelve Sautéed Matsutake. Don't wanna overdo it.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Anyone else wanna add something? Or we could just start there and add stuff later...

choices.text: That's plenty.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like Varesa's appetite is as crazy as ever... Thanks, Sara, that'll do for now.

response.speaker: Sara
response.text: A—Are you sure it's not too much...?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, I promise you, none of it will go to waste.

response.speaker: Sara
response.text: Uh, if you say so... Well then. I guess I'd better get cooking...

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Hehe, nothing beats eating a nice big meal when you're hungry for it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After a short wait, Sara expertly maneuvers the enormous platter of dishes to your tables.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "Thanks!" says Varesa, before digging in like there's no tomorrow.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: No matter how many times I witness it, the Varesa VS Food show never ceases to amaze me. You gotta hand it to the Collective of Plenty: They can pack it away, and they can pack a punch.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Well, you gotta eat so you have enough energy for training... And as Fietena once said, "Even a beast of the Abyss knows that being a picky eater... is an unpardonable sin!" So, all the more reason for us to eat our fill.

response.speaker: Alrani
response.text: Ooh, I know that line. It's from that standalone special, Fietena VS Abyss Lector: Battle of the Meat Feasters. Right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wow. Really plumbing the depths of obscurity here...

response.speaker: Alrani
response.text: Don't underestimate a hardcore fan. I know every line in The Soulblazer Saga, no matter where in the Soulblazer universe it comes from.

response.speaker: Tang Yigang
response.text: Haha, nice one, Alrani. The writers had fun with that one, didn't they? Pure comedy.

response.speaker: Tang Yigang
response.text: Can you imagine if that was based on a true story? Haha... an eating competition with an Abyssal monster — such a hilarious proposition.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Yeah, it's really stretching the boundaries of possibilities. I guess it takes a certain kind of talent to come up with ideas like that.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Wacky ideas are one thing, but what really blows my mind is the characterization process.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: The way they take historical figures like Fietena and breathe new life into them as comic-book heroes is just so impressive.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: "Some people think I'm not enough. I have two words for those people: Think again."

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: That's one of my favorite Fietena quotes of all time.

response.speaker: Alrani
response.text: That's from the Soulblazer Saga, volume 3. Just FYI.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Thanks, Alrani.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Minnie, do you have a favorite Soulblazer quote? Or a favorite plot point in general?

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: I think for me... it's the way they portray Fietena's dream.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Despite the endless numbers of monsters, and even when the Abyss seems like a never-ending threat, Fietena never gives up fighting for her dream homeland.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Ahem... "Maybe it is impossible. But if we don't try, we'll never know."

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Ah, yeah, I love that line too!

response.speaker: Alrani
response.text: Volume 3 strikes again. FYI.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: No matter what, Fietena always stays true to her dreams. That's why she'll always be my favorite hero.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Same... But when I look at my own life, I wonder... Will I ever have that same kind of tireless dedication? Following your dreams is so hard sometimes.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: I feel like I'm giving everything I have to give, but everyone around me is telling me "give up, it's not realistic"... Ugh, I don't know. Honestly, I'm not even that good of an artist. I'm never quite happy with my work.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Sometimes, I get to thinking that I should just pack my pens and paper away and be done with it. Maybe life would be easier that way.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: But I've tried that before too... and it's never long before I start to miss it. I'll be at the grocery store buying some cured meat, or at home doing some chores, and I'll suddenly find myself thinking... "I miss my art."

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Lemme guess, it always ends up with you digging out your art supplies and giving it another try?

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Yeah. It's turning into a bit of a cycle, honestly. I keep flip-flopping between "that's it, I'm never painting again!" and "no, I gotta keep trying!"

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Who am I kidding. I'll never have Fietena's perseverance.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: You're thinking about it all wrong, Minnie. Even Fietena had days when she didn't feel like training or eating right!

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Having tireless dedication doesn't mean doing the same thing on repeat every day.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: To me, dedication just means being passionate about something. Wherever you go, whatever you do, you always carry it in your heart.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Sometimes you let yourself go, but it's okay. You can always get back on the wagon. If you lose muscle or stamina, you just build it back up again.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: The important thing is to keep that passion alive through all the ups and downs! As Fietena said...

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: "There is only one eternal power in this world... the power of love."

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Exactly! From volume 6, when Fietena delivers the crushing blow to her enemies. You see? The important lessons stay with you.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Yeah... And they always will.

choices.text: Here's to your dreams.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait a sec! Varesa, when did you clear all those plates!?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: While everyone was talking. I guess Fietena put me in the mood for a meat feast.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No fair! C'mon everyone, eat! We need to catch up!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everyone grabs their cutlery and vies for a fair share of the remaining food.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So full... Uhhh...

response.speaker: Tang Yigang
response.text: I can't eat another bite... I'm absolutely stuffed.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Should we head back to camp? We can walk off some of that food.

choices.text: Here's to your passion.
We can always order more if we need.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: There's no more group activities today. Once we get back to camp, everyone's free to do their own thing.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: That's a relief. I'm about to go into a food coma.

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: Ah, Minnie! Where have you been? I've been looking everywhere for you!

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Patton...? What is it? Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: What do you think? You've been gone for days and haven't checked in once. Mom and dad are worried.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: I—I've been out training for the race with my friends all morning. We just got back, and everyone was hungry so we came to get some food.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Mom and dad should know about it, though... I told them, I've signed up for a cross country contest, and I'll be at Dragonspine practicing in the days leading up to it... They agreed and everything...

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: Yeah, well... You know what they're like. They agree at first, but then several days go by without seeing you, and now they're freaking out. It's always that way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, so Patton from the tavern is your brother?

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: Are these the friends you were telling me about? ...Wait, Honorary Knight!?

choices.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: Hey, everyone. I'm Minnie's much older brother.

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: When did you make friends with the Honorary Knight, Minnie? You kept that one quiet.

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Oh, uh... Well, the Honorary Knight just sort of showed up for the pre-race training. I never had the chance to tell you guys.

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: Thanks for taking care of Minnie, everyone. I hope she hasn't been too much trouble...?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Don't be silly! Minnie's our good friend. We've been hanging out, training together... it's been super fun!

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: Good, glad to hear it. Okay, well... Mom and dad said to tell you they miss you, and they hope you come home soon.

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: It's great that you've got a hobby you're so passionate about, but don't let it take up all your time, okay? You gotta come home and check in once in a while.

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: Come home as soon as you can, okay? You can go back to training tomorrow. We don't want mom and dad blowing a gasket...

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Okay, I get it...

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: I'm heading back to the camp with my friends now, but once we get there, I'll grab my luggage and head home.

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: Okay, great. Make it quick, though. Otherwise, mom and dad will probably go all the way to Dragonspine looking for you...

response.speaker: Patton
response.text: Sorry to intrude, everyone. Have a great day — I'd better get back to the tavern now.

choices.text: Hey, Patton.

talks.objective: Return to the camp with your teammates

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Achoo... Man, I almost forgot how cold the mountain was. The difference between here and the city is mind-boggling. I'm gonna go warm up in the tent.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: I'll join you. Right now, I just wanna wrap myself in blankets and let the food coma run its course.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: I'd better come too, so I can grab my luggage...

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: Minnie!

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: There you are, young lady...

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Mom, Dad... You actually came...

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: What choice did we have? When were you planning on coming home? I thought this was supposed to only last a couple of days, but you've been gone for most of the week!

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: I never said a couple of days... I said several days.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: You did, I remember that. But we also agreed that you'd be out during the days and come back home every night. Come on, it's time to go.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: ...Okay. I'll just let my friends know.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Hey guys, I won't be staying in the camp tonight. See you tomorrow for training.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: I'm sorry? Tomorrow as well? This is all getting to be a bit too much, Minnie...

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: You've been out here for days on end. Don't you think you've had your fun? Besides, you're not built for this cold weather.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: Remember that dreadful fever you had as a child? It took the better part of a week to clear up. Your mother and I worried ourselves half to death about you.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Hello, Sir. I'm Minnie's friend, Varesa.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: Ah, Varesa, how do you do... I believe Minnie's mentioned you before. Thank you for keeping her company out here. *sigh* Sorry, I would have brought a welcome gift if I'd known...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Welcome gift? Nooo, there's no need for that! I just wanted to say, this contest... it really means a lot to Minnie. We've been training together in preparation for it.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Minnie's taking the training really seriously. Every day, she starts earlier and finishes later than anyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Whether it's strength training or practicing out on the race course, she's been working the hardest out of everyone in our group.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Didn't you make a deal with her? I heard that as long as Minnie gets ranked in the contest, you'll consider letting her do what she wants with her life.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Her greatest wish is to work in the comic book industry, and she's putting so much work into it. Surely you don't want to see all her efforts go to waste?

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: Of course not, but the thing is...

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Mom, I...

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: That's enough! What's more important, your comics or your health?

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: I don't know how many times we've told you: It's great that you have a hobby, but you need to learn the difference between work and play.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: When's it going to stop, Minnie? When you ruin your health in the name of fun?

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: Don't take your father's words too hard, Minnie. Both of us just want what's best for you.

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: You're still young, and it's great that you have something you're passionate about. But at some point, you need to think about your future.

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: I've seen your artwork, and I do think you have a wonderful talent. But being a comic book artist just isn't a stable career.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* I'm sorry, Minnie, I didn't mean to be so harsh.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: I know how much effort you're putting into this — we both do. We really admire your determination... You're our daughter, and we love you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: But surely, you can appreciate where we're coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: Dreams are great. But at the end of the day, they don't put food on the table.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Mom, Dad, can we please continue this in private?

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: Yes, of course. Let's move over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Things got pretty intense with Minnie's parents there. Even Paimon didn't dare to interrupt...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Yeah. I kinda wanted to speak up on Minnie's behalf again, but I didn't even know how to butt in...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I mean, it sounded like their hearts are in the right place. They said they have her best interests in mind, expressed concern for her health, tried to comfort her...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: But the whole thing still just felt kinda off to me. I can't quite pinpoint what it was, though...

choices.text: What about your parents, Varesa?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Huh? Is that a trick question? Don't all parents support their children...?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: I mean... Whether I'm training, eating, or heading to bed for a nap, they're all smiles.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: But Minnie's parents... neither of them were smiling when they spoke to her just now.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Their words were caring, but their tone was so angry... I don't understand it.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: It sounds like they don't wanna let Minnie take part in the contest... But then all her hard work will have been for nothing! What are we gonna do?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: *sigh*... I'm supposed to be Minnie's captain, but I feel powerless to help her...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: ...Heh, I wasn't expecting Nepecha's gift for Minnie to come in handy so soon.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I was planning to save it as a final surprise before we leave, but under the circumstances, it would be silly not to use it now...

choices.text: You've got a plan, Xilonen?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I can't put smiles on her parents' faces. But I think I can make sure Minnie gets to participate in the contest.

choices.text: How do we fix this?
Have they always supported you?

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: That's not true... I promise, I would never...

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: Well, in that case, we can discuss this more back home.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt, but there's something I'd like to discuss with the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: You must be... Vice Captain Xilonen? Minnie's mentioned you before.... Is something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: If it's about the competition, don't worry — we'll let Minnie take part. But as we've just informed her, this will be her last time. We don't want her wasting any more time on worthless pursuits.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Gotcha... Look, I don't mean to interfere with your family business, but Minnie's a part of our team. I have to make sure everyone's in the right frame of mind to compete.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: And I can't help but feel that her conversation with you was a little demotivating. I'm concerned it's gonna impact her performance on race day.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I also don't think you're really validating her efforts when you brand something your daughter is passionate about as "wasting time."

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Like I said, not trying to intrude on your family business or anything. But I thought you should know that a student of mine back home simply adores Minnie's artwork.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: She's not here to speak for herself, but as her teacher, I felt like I should pass along the message.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: I agree that Minnie has artistic talent, but I stand by what I said earlier. Hobbies are hobbies, work is work. A couple of fans isn't going to get you anywhere in life...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yeah, about that... Take a look at this letter.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: ...What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Let's call it a token of appreciation from Minnie's fanbase.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: They wanted to write one letter each, but I told them I couldn't take a whole sack of mail on a long-distance trip.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: So instead, my student Nepecha arranged for them all to make a group painting for Minnie.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: In the end, so many people participated that it was pretty much one brush-stroke per person.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Nepecha's so thoughtful...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Sorry, Minnie, Nepecha wanted me to give this to you as a surprise after the competition.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But given the situation, I made the executive decision to give it to you now.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: So... So how many people is this?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You think Minnie's wasting her time because in your eyes, making art isn't a worthwhile job.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: And when you use words like "worthless," what you're really saying is, it's not a stable source of income. Am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: ...Yes. You're right.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Well, now you have another way to measure "worth." Your daughter's artwork has attracted a whole lot of fans, and very enthusiastic ones at that.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Since arriving in Mondstadt, I've learned that being a bard is seen as a very respectable profession here.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Let's imagine Minnie was a bard for a second. Instead of drawings and paintings, she'd produce poetry and songs. Instead of fans, she'd have an audience.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Would you still be inclined to stop her from being creative? Would lyrics and music be just as much of a "waste of time"?

dialogues.speaker: Sherilyn
dialogues.text: I take your point, but there's still the issue of her health...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Sorry... lemme butt in real quick! You know, Minnie's not nearly as fragile as you think.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I'm not just saying that, either. I've been doing competitive sports in my tribe since I was a little kid, so I know what I'm talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Sure, Minnie's not built like a pro bodybuilder, but she's got great potential.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: A sensible amount of exercise is good for her health. Far better than staying cooped up at home all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Mom, Dad... My health is a lot better these days. Really. I feel great.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Now that I'm training every day, my appetite's improved and I'm sleeping better.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: Minnie... Sometimes I forget how grown up you are now. You're your own person with your own ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: To tell you the truth, your mother and I don't really understand this whole world of comics and Yae Publishing House.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: *sigh* When all's said and done... We just want you to have a safe and stable life. The last thing we want is to see you suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Moritz
dialogues.text: But a deal is a deal... This competition clearly means a lot to you. So, give it your best shot. See it through to the end.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! I will!

choices.text: Don't worry.

response.speaker: Moritz
response.text: Thank you, Honorary Knight. It really does ease my mind knowing that you're on the team.

response.speaker: Moritz
response.text: Heh, I think I've said enough for one day. Minnie, you're free to attend training and attend the competition, but you're not to stay out at night. Come home and sleep in your own bed. Understand?

response.speaker: Minnie
response.text: Yes, Dad!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Minnie collects her luggage and leaves with her parents. They promise to bring her to tomorrow's training session.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: ...Phew, at least we got there in the end.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your powers of persuasion worked like a charm!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Heh. It was a shot in the dark, honestly... I'm not good at dealing with family drama. Sure as heck didn't have a Plan B, so it's a good thing the letter worked.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: This is way more than I signed up for. I only came here to buy that... merch stuff or whatever.

choices.text: Even though it wasn't what you signed up for...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, you think? I dunno, seeing how Minnie's parents were acting, it just reminded me of a similar situation from a while back.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Sometimes, someone can love their idea of another person so much that they'll try to mold them to fit that mental image.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But if "love" is starting to restrict your freedom, it's time to get out.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Anyway, Minnie's parents aren't nearly that extreme.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Let's go get ready. Tomorrow is race day, and we have to deliver results.

choices.text: You really rose to the occasion.
I'll make sure Minnie gets through this safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Minnie and Family
dialogues.text: (Minnie is talking with her parents. The atmosphere seems very stern.)

dialogues.speaker: Minnie
dialogues.text: What's the weather like in Natlan? I bet it's hotter than here?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Haha, what kind of a question is that? Everywhere's hotter than here!

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: Yigang, which book are you gonna borrow?

dialogues.speaker: Tang Yigang
dialogues.text: Just this one, Armored Assault, volume 1. Can't beat the classics.
